messages.author: 6667ef04b386b9ec
messages.subject: General questions about parallelization
parts:
Hi There!

I have a code not parallelized working on and I want to run it in parallel. My questions are:

1. Do I only need to change Type nll = 0; by parallel_accumulator<Type> nll(this);?
2. Is there any extra trick for models with random effects? (I haven't seen any parallel code for random effect model in the book);
3. My random effect model usually has two different for() with two different sizes that evaluate my nll (negative log likelihood). Is it a problem?
4. To use benchmark function, my obj needs to be from a parallelized model? (If so, I think that it would be nice to include it in the description of the obj).

5. How does benchmark work? (It evaluates the obj from MakeADFun for every number of cores "n" times in a given "random" point?)
6. What is the gray line in the plot.parallelBenchmark? (Would it be the overall time?)
7. Can I control the number of cores used in parallel? (The default is to use all processors, I think).

I got this these questions in mind when I started running models in parallel with TMB.
Where for the first 4 I have an answer in mind (Yes, No, No, Yes), and last 3 in blue I don't.

If anyone can contribute, I would appreciate that.

Obs: I was able to run a Beta longitudinal regression model with both intercept and slope for fixed and random effects, whereas the random effects are correlated. I just want to make sure that my "empirical" learning (trial and error) is correct, because I will need to use it for other models.

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: General questions about parallelization
parts:
Hi,

Regarding your (1)-(3) I think you are correct, but I cannot say for sure.
I agree that there is a need to state exact rules in the documentation.

For your (7) I have used "TMB:::openmp(32)" in R, and empirically verified that the program
utilizes 32 cores.

Hans
